source: Chrysikou, Weber, Thompson-Schill (2014) A matched filter hypothesis for cognitive control
finding: Control is a tool for some tasks, not a general optimiser. High control suits explicit, rule-based, verbal tasks that fit in working memory. Low control (hypofrontality) suits implicit, reward-based, nonverbal tasks that exceed working memory.
numbers: Probability matching example: adults pick the 75% option 75% of the time (62.5% expected success); children pick it 100% of the time (75% expected success). Dual-task, DLPFC TMS and secondary tasks helped implicit learning (Brown & Robertson 2007; Galea 2010).
quote: a tool adapted to a subset of common challenges
limits: Read the first 100k of 233k characters. Direct adult creativity evidence is sparse and the author says several links are untested. No effect sizes for the creativity tDCS study.
agent_relevance: Control level is a per-task setting. Use high control for rule tasks and verification, lower control for open generation (O4). Not one global dial.

source: Chrysikou, Weber, Thompson-Schill (2014) A matched filter hypothesis for cognitive control (creativity evidence section)
finding: Cites creative-use generation with lower PFC and higher perceptual-region activity than typical-use generation (Chrysikou & Thompson-Schill 2011). Cites inhibitory tDCS on left PFC speeding up and increasing creative-use output (Chrysikou 2013). Children are less fixated than adults.
numbers: No numbers given in the review. Per the Rosen 2016 summary, cathodal left PFC cut reaction times and omissions in the uncommon-uses condition only.
limits: Second-hand summary of small tDCS studies. The review says evaluating ideas still needs PFC control and that transitions between states are not specified.
agent_relevance: Relaxing control helps novelty only in the generation step. Keep a controlled evaluation step after it.

source: Rosen et al. (2016) Anodal tDCS to right DLPFC facilitates performance for novice jazz improvisers but hinders experts
finding: No main effect of anodal or cathodal tDCS over right DLPFC. A strong stimulation-by-expertise interaction: more control helped novices and hurt experts. Expertise is a moderator of the best control level.
numbers: 17 pianists, 102 rated improvisations (34 per condition), 1.5 mA for 15 min. Interaction estimate -0.24, SE 0.08, p = 0.002. Least experienced +0.91 (SE 0.32, p = 0.004). Most experienced -0.54 (SE 0.20, p = 0.007). In sham, +0.80 rating per unit of expertise.
quote: stimulation benefitted musicians with less experience but hindered those with more experience
limits: Small sample. Authors say it needs replication and may overestimate effects. Almost all male. No replication found in my search.
agent_relevance: Expertise changes the best control level. In a new domain keep checks on. Where routines are strong, loosen control.

source: Rosen et al. (2016) introduction: state of the tDCS creativity literature
finding: States the tDCS creativity literature offers 'little clear evidence' that it enhances creativity. Lists early small positive findings (Chi & Snyder insight; Colombo 2015 left DLPFC; Green 2016 frontopolar analogy) and the Limb & Braun jazz fMRI result of PFC deactivation.
numbers: Colombo 2015: N = 45, 3 groups, 1.5 mA, 20 min. Zmigrod 2015: N = 28 (14 per experiment). Chi & Snyder 2011: N = 60, about three times more insight solutions (as quoted by Rosen).
limits: Early stimulation studies are small and mostly unreplicated. Limb & Braun 2008 was not opened, only cited through this paper.
agent_relevance: Treat 'prefrontal off equals more creative' as a weak, task-dependent claim, not a rule.

source: Gong et al. (2023) A positive association between working memory capacity and human creativity: meta-analytic evidence
finding: Working memory capacity correlates only weakly with creativity. More control capacity helps a little. The effect is similar for verbal, visuospatial and dual-task WM.
limits: Small effect. Mixed creativity measures. Moderator contrasts are between-study.
agent_relevance: Raw control capacity is a weak predictor. A longer context or more working memory will not by itself buy creativity.

source: Gong et al. (2023) publication bias and quality
finding: Funnel plot symmetric and Egger test not significant, so small-study bias is unlikely for the weak WM-creativity link. Study quality acceptable.
numbers: Egger e = .449, p = .350. mNOS mean 4.65 (SD 0.56). Heterogeneity I2 = 55% overall, 39% to 70% in subgroups.
limits: Only 28 studies. Heterogeneity not explained by the moderators tested.
agent_relevance: The small WM-creativity effect is probably real, not a bias artefact.

source: Gong et al. (2023) culture and age as moderators
finding: Culture moderated the link between WM and creativity (stronger in Asian samples). Age did not.
limits: Small k per cell, confounded by task and sample.
agent_relevance: Effects of control differ by population. Calibrate any control setting on the target task mix.

source: Meta-analysis of working memory capacity and creativity (Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 2023)
finding: A larger meta-analysis found WM capacity relates more strongly to convergent than to divergent creative thinking.
numbers: 525 correlations, 79 studies, 12,846 participants (search snippet only).
limits: Not opened: the page redirected to a login check. Authors and effect sizes not verified.
agent_relevance: Fits the pattern that control helps rule-bound, convergent steps more than open generation.

source: Chen et al. (2024) A meta-analysis of the effects of tDCS on creative thinking (Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts)
finding: Small positive effect of anodal tDCS on creative performance, none for cathodal. Anodal helped convergent but not divergent thinking overall. Left DLPFC anodal helped both. Left IFG anodal reduced creative performance.
numbers: 32 studies, 125 effect sizes, about 1,538 participants (search summary).
limits: Not opened (paywalled; seen only through a search summary). Subgroups small. Conflicts with a simple 'switch off PFC' story.
agent_relevance: More activity in left DLPFC helped. So hypofrontality is not general. Do not rely on a simple 'less control' rule.

source: Pena et al. (2022) tDCS vs tRNS over left DLPFC and left IFG: effects on divergent and convergent thinking
finding: Double-blind, sham-controlled. Overall tests mostly null. Only picture completion differed by group, driven by tRNS over sham. Unusual uses did not differ.
numbers: N = 66 (22 per group), 1.5 mA, 20 min. Picture completion F = 3.35, p = .042, np2 = .10; tRNS vs sham p = .004 (fluency p = .012, originality p = .021). Unusual uses F = 0.61, p = .546. RAT F = 2.65, p = .079 (tDCS vs sham p = .038, exploratory).
limits: Small groups. Several tests with no correction I could find. Anode left DLPFC with cathode left IFG, so the two sites are confounded.
agent_relevance: The cleanest recent stimulation test finds weak or null effects. Weak support for engineering around a prefrontal switch.

source: Pena et al. (2022) cognitive flexibility and side effects
finding: Stroop-measured cognitive flexibility did not change with any stimulation, so no mediation analysis was run. The tDCS group reported more side effects, which weakens blinding.
numbers: Stroop F = 0.34, p = .711. Adverse effects F = 3.46, p = .035; tDCS M = 2.18 (SD 1.70) vs sham M = 1.29 (SD 1.34), p = .015.
limits: Mediation test not possible; N = 66 is low power.
agent_relevance: A control gain measured on Stroop did not transfer to idea quality. Do not assume it will.

source: Khalil et al. (2023) Individual differences and creative ideation: neuromodulatory signatures of mindset and response inhibition
finding: Effect of left/right IFG tDCS on divergent thinking depends on response inhibition (go/no-go d') and mindset. Growth mindset moderated effects, with opposite signs for fluency and flexibility. Originality was unaffected.
numbers: N = 40 (19 vs 21). Left-IFG: inhibition to flexibility b = 0.477, SE 0.205, p = .034 at high mindset; mindset x inhibition on flexibility p = .036. Right-IFG: fluency interaction p = .017.
limits: Secondary analysis of the 2020 data. Small N, many models. Mindset is self-report.
agent_relevance: The effect of loosening depends on a baseline control trait. For an agent, the best setting depends on that model's default behaviour.

source: Khalil et al. (2020), as reported in Khalil 2023: IFG tDCS and inhibition
finding: Earlier study: tDCS raised originality and flexibility (not fluency) in the right-anodal, left-cathodal condition, and only when go/no-go d' was high.
numbers: Same N = 40 data. No separate statistics here.
limits: Second-hand through the 2023 paper. The 2020 paper was not opened.
agent_relevance: Inhibition ability gates whether a loosening intervention works.

source: Attentional inhibition and cognitive flexibility in convergent and divergent thinking (2026, two experiments, University of Lancashire)
finding: Control predicts convergent thinking (compound remote associates) strongly and divergent thinking only weakly. Inhibition predicted alternative-uses originality but not fluency or flexibility.
numbers: Exp 1 N = 55: incongruent accuracy predicts CRAT b = 0.106, p = .031 and AUT originality b = 1.77, p = .013 (R2 = .16). Fluency F(3,51) = 0.18, p = .908. Flexibility p = .41. Exp 2 N = 49: flanker RT costs explained 56% of CRAT variance and 52% of originality (adjusted R2).
limits: Very high R2 in samples of 49 to 55 needs caution. One university. Self-reported strategy.
agent_relevance: Control helps the analytic, rule-bound solve. For open idea lists extra control adds little. Apply control at convergent steps.

source: Same 2026 flanker study: strategy and flexibility moderators
finding: Control mattered most for remote-associate items solved by analysis, as self-reported. The Wisconsin Card Sort predicted CRAT beyond the flanker measures. Authors support a 'business-as-usual' view for convergent tasks.
numbers: Power: 52 needed for d = 0.5, 55 recruited in Exp 1. Exp 2 (N = 49) power .77 for r about .48.
limits: Retrospective strategy reports are unreliable.
agent_relevance: Insight-type steps depend less on control than analytic steps. Route by step type.

source: Zabelina et al. (2016) Dopamine and the creative mind: interactions between COMT and DAT genes
finding: No main effects of frontal (COMT) or striatal (DAT) dopamine genes on creativity, only an interaction. Divergent-thinking scores were best with flexible plus medium top-down control, or weak flexibility plus strong control. Real-world achievement was best with weak control and weak flexibility.
numbers: N = 100. DAT x COMT on ATTA F(2,67) = 4.28, p = .02, partial eta2 = .12. Creative achievement F(2,69) = 4.21, p = .02. Fluency: no effects, p > .36.
limits: Candidate-gene interaction, a design with a poor replication record. One sample, mostly university students with artistic achievement.
agent_relevance: Best control is non-monotonic and depends on flexibility and persistence together. Treat it as a trade-off, not a maximum.

source: Lucchiari, Sala, Vanutelli (2018) Promoting creativity through tDCS: a critical review
finding: Review of 18 tDCS creativity studies finds results 'confusing and inconsistent'. Proposes a creative on/off model: relax inhibitory control to generate, engage DMN and DLPFC to select.
numbers: 48 articles found, 14 eligible plus 4 added = 18. Typical samples: Colombo 2015 N = 45; Zmigrod 2015 N = 28; Mayseless 2015 two experiments of N = 30; Chi & Snyder 2011 N = 60.
limits: Narrative review, no pooled effect size. Many studies tiny and not preregistered.
agent_relevance: Supports a two-phase loop: loosen control to generate, tighten it to select.

source: Chan, Lambon Ralph, Robinson (2026) The neural basis of creative thought: an ALE meta-analysis of 787 experiments (Cortex)
finding: Brain regions used in creativity tasks overlap heavily with regions for semantic knowledge and executive control. Creative thought looks like general mechanisms combined, not a separate creativity module.
numbers: 787 experiments, 10,357 foci, 17,228 healthy adults.
limits: Abstract only (via Europe PMC record). Reverse-inference limits. Does not show how control and default systems trade off over time.
agent_relevance: Do not build a separate creativity module. Combine knowledge retrieval and executive control in the loop.

source: Barnett et al. (2025) Enhanced DMN-executive network connectivity during flow states (review)
finding: Argues good creative states couple default and control networks rather than switching one off. In a cited Tetris/Pong study, optimal difficulty gave the most flow and the most right frontoparietal activity.
numbers: No pooled numbers. Cited study: easy, optimal, hard, self-selected difficulty conditions.
limits: Narrative review, mostly correlational. Only part of the text was read.
agent_relevance: Cooperation of generate and control systems beats pure relaxation. Match task difficulty to skill.

source: Huang, Liu, Yang (2026) Evaluation of LLMs as tools, models and partners in creative thinking research (GCA review)
finding: LLMs beat average humans on divergent-thinking tests, yet there is no evidence they use human-like creative mechanisms. Mapping human individual-difference variables such as WM and openness onto LLM behaviour gave inconsistent results.
numbers: LLM advantage Hedges' g = 0.52 to 2.61 across four independent comparisons. Humans win at the peak level. Automated scoring ICC >= 0.80 and r >= 0.70 in selected studies.
limits: Selective narrative review, no pooling. Results depend on prompt and fluency control.
agent_relevance: An LLM has no prefrontal-default trade-off. Any 'control' knob must be built from prompts, sampling and verifier steps and then tested.

source: Huang, Liu, Yang (2026): temperature and decoding as the nearest LLM analogue
finding: Temperature raises lower-probability tokens and diversity at the cost of coherence. Top-p balances the two. Explicit diversity objectives exist. These are the controllable analogue of relaxing constraints.
numbers: No pooled numbers. Output is a function of the model plus the prompt, so each result is conditional on the prompt.
limits: Analogy only. No study here tests prefrontal-style control directly in a model.
agent_relevance: Sampling temperature is a rough hypofrontality dial. Pair it with a verifier.

source: Wenger et al. (2026) Large language models are homogeneously creative (PNAS Nexus)
finding: 22 LLMs give far more similar creative answers to each other than 102 humans do. Mean originality is similar. Raising temperature raises variety, but at T = 2.0 outputs were largely gibberish.
numbers: 102 humans, 22 LLMs, three tasks (AUT, DAT, forward flow). LLMs slightly above humans on AUT and DAT originality, below on forward flow. Temperatures 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 tested. T = 2.0 responses had to be culled by hand rules.
limits: Single-turn tasks. Not tied to any neural control theory.
agent_relevance: Loosening by temperature widens variety only until coherence breaks. Use a sampler plus a filter, and diversity across models, not only high T.

source: Horowitz-Kraus et al. (2026) Lower engagement of cognitive control in children on ChatGPT
finding: With ChatGPT as co-creator, creativity scores matched between 6-7-year-olds and adults, but adults showed stronger frontoparietal, salience and dorsal-attention connectivity.
numbers: 15 children, 16 adults, fMRI. DAT children 28.61 (SD 19.59) vs adults 26.16 (SD 21.53), NS. Moderation FP-salience F(1,26) = 5.869, p = .023, partial eta2 = .184. Adult slope +0.028 per 1 SD creativity.
limits: Very small sample. Cross-sectional. Age and AI use confounded.
agent_relevance: Similar outputs can come with less control engagement, so an LLM partner may substitute for human control. Check outputs, not process.

source: Matched filter (2014): developmental and individual boundary conditions
finding: Benefits of low control depend on task type, developmental stage, genotype and dopamine level. For reversal learning the dopamine relation is an inverted U.
numbers: No effect sizes. Children show less blocking, highlighting and functional fixedness than adults (Sobel 2004; German & Defeyter 2000).
limits: Mostly indirect evidence.
agent_relevance: The dial is non-linear. Too little or too much control both harm.

source: Synthesis of lines b01 to b24: rival accounts of control and creativity
finding: Three rival readings. (1) Control blocks creativity (hypofrontality). (2) Control is a business-as-usual helper (flanker data). (3) Creativity is general parts combined (ALE). Data favour 2 and 3 for convergent tasks and leave 1 for narrow cases such as the novice/expert split and implicit tasks.
numbers: Discriminating numbers: WM r = .083 (k = 28); ALE 787 experiments; tDCS meta 32 studies with left DLPFC anodal helping; Rosen interaction p = .002 (17 pianists).
limits: This line is my synthesis of lines already listed, not a new source.
agent_relevance: Choose control per step and per model skill. No single prefrontal-style setting wins.
